title: Buddha Jayanti Park Delhi - Attractions, Timings & Travel Guide
content:
Buddha Jayanti Park - Delhi,

Buddha Jayanti Park in Delhi is a serene green retreat located in the heart of the city, close to Ridge Road. Built to commemorate the 2,500th anniversary of Lord Buddha’s enlightenment, the park is known for its calm environment, lush lawns, and the grand Buddha statue placed at the center. It is a popular spot for peaceful walks, meditation, family picnics, and enjoying nature away from city noise.

History:

The park was inaugurated in 1964 by then Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri to honor the life and teachings of Lord Buddha. A sapling of the Bodhi tree from Sri Lanka, which itself comes from the original tree in Bodh Gaya, was also planted here, adding to the park’s spiritual significance.

  • Attractions at Buddha Jayanti Park:
  • Buddha Statue – A tall and peaceful statue of Lord Buddha surrounded by greenery.
  • Bodhi Tree Sapling – A sacred tree planted here, believed to be a descendant of the original Bodhi tree.
  • Walking & Jogging Tracks – Long paths shaded by trees, ideal for morning and evening walks.
  • Floral Gardens – Seasonal flowers and well-maintained lawns perfect for photography.
  • Picnic Areas – Open lawns where families and friends gather for a peaceful day out.

Visitor Information:

  • Location: Ridge Road, Central Delhi.
  • Timings: 5:00 AM – 7:00 PM (all days).
  • Entry Fee: Free.
  • Parking: Available near the main entrance of the park.

How to Reach:

  • By Metro: Nearest metro station is Rajiv Chowk (Blue/Yellow Line), about 4 km away. You can take an auto or cab from there.
  • By Bus: Regular DTC buses stop near Ridge Road and Shankar Road.
  • By Car/Taxi: Easily accessible via Ridge Road; cabs and autos are convenient.

Best Time to Visit: The park can be visited throughout the year, but the October to March season is most enjoyable for outdoor activities and walks, thanks to the pleasant weather.

Nearby Attractions:

  • Delhi Ridge (adjacent)
  • Raj Ghat (6 km)
  • India Gate (7 km)
  • Connaught Place (4 km)

Travel Tips: Carry a mat or picnic basket if you’re planning to spend a few hours here—it’s one of the most relaxing picnic spots in Delhi.
excerpt: The Buddha Jayanti Park in Delhi is a peaceful green oasis dedicated to Lord Buddha. With its statue, Bodhi tree sapling, and wide lawns, it’s perfect for meditation, morning walks, or a family picnic.
